clue.text: Puzzled, needing source of inspiration in the sack

indicators.note: the inspiring figure is placed in the sack, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack'
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A baffled writer heads to bed, hoping inspiration will strike there.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bemused is bewildered or confused, a close synonym of puzzled.

clue.text: Change into suit

definitions.meaning: to turn into or develop into
to look good on, as a colour may flatter someone

explanation.surface: Put on a different outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar may turn into a butterfly; and a dress can flatter its wearer: both senses of the word.

clue.text: Threat from expert supporting workers

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: men are workers, as in management and men
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Danger arises when a specialist backs the labour force.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or something that intimidates, a close synonym of threat.

clue.text: Outline design of hotel suite

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so these letters are recomposed

explanation.surface: A sketch of the plan for a hotel's rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is the dark shape or outline of something seen against light.

clue.text: Style of building seen in Finland (or Iceland)

indicators.note: seen in means the letters are visible within these words

explanation.surface: An architectural style found in the Nordic countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, a style with plain columns.

clue.text: Run from vehicles on the road

definitions.meaning: to run goods is to deal in them illicitly, as in trafficking drugs
the cars and lorries moving along a road collectively

explanation.surface: Someone flees from the cars and lorries on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafficking means trading illegally, like running guns; and the flow of cars on a road is its everyday sense.

clue.text: Thinking of making contact?

parts.note: reads as considering getting in touch, but describes reaching another mind by thought alone

explanation.surface: Someone is considering getting in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinking of' reads as considering, but it is contact made by means of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is supposed communication between minds without speech or signals.

clue.text: A million visiting church for summit

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so this piece enters the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rich person stops at a church on the way to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement, a synonym of summit.

clue.text: Acted nervously seeing unusually gifted newspaper leader

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: ED, an editor, leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A talented editor was seen squirming with nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to make small restless movements, as a nervous person does.

clue.text: Settler working one's time under officer

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit below the officer, so they follow it

parts.note: COL is short for colonel
on means working, as a machine is on
I is one, so one's is IS

explanation.surface: A pioneer doing their service under a commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist is someone who settles in a new country or colony.

clue.text: Article found in mostly peaceful stretch of water

indicators.note: the article is found inside the other word, so one piece sits within the other
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: peaceful means calm
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item discovered in a quiet stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway, a long stretch of water cut for boats.

clue.text: A good example of register incorporating European fashion

indicators.note: incorporating means taking something into the body of the word, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a roll is a register or list of names
mode means fashion, as in 'a la mode'

explanation.surface: A list that brings in European fashion sets a good example.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and imitate, a good example to follow.

clue.text: Viewer offering very little opportunity?

parts.note: micro means very small, as a prefix or an adjective
scope means room or opportunity to act

explanation.surface: A spectator who gives almost no chance of anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' reads as a person watching, but it is an instrument for viewing; the question mark flags the split into very little plus opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is an optical instrument through which tiny things are viewed.

clue.text: Head started to lose heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: started means began

explanation.surface: A leader began to feel discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To lose heart' removes the central G of BEGAN. 'Bean' is informal slang for a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is old slang for the head, as in 'use your bean'.

clue.text: Unsolicited opinion from writer thrown out across yard

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: across means lying over the other piece, so it surrounds it
out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An author's uninvited view was ejected over the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' scrambles THROWN to NWORTH; 'across' puts it round Y after the N. To put in one's two pennyworth is to offer unasked-for views.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone giving their two pennyworth offers a view nobody asked for, the British idiom behind the definition.

clue.text: All the same shelters, even in a storm

indicators.note: things caught in a storm are tossed about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Even so, the shelters are still standing in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: All the same is an idiom meaning however or in spite of that, the same sense as this word.

clue.text: European jet fighter valued for what 8 did

parts.note: MiG is the Russian jet fighter aircraft
valued means rated

explanation.surface: A prized European warplane, as the settler had done.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the settler of 8-down, who left home for a new country.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler typically left their homeland to live abroad, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Old and battered car oddly dumped in river — mine

indicators.note: something dumped in a river goes into it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-positioned letters of car

parts.note: a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit

explanation.surface: An old wreck of a car, dumped in a river beside a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives C and R from 'car', which go inside DEE, a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes something worn out and weakened by age, like an old battered car.

clue.text: Measure, including most of additional sugar

indicators.note: including means holding the other piece within

parts.note: a dose is a measured amount of medicine

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: extra means additional

explanation.surface: A spoonful with a little extra sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is a form of glucose, a simple sugar.

clue.text: Rice, if gently cooked, will be astounding

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or doctored, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef promises that rice simmered gently will amaze diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrifying describes something thrilling or startling, much like astounding.

clue.text: Pressure in heavy defeats lifted daze

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means turned upwards, so read backwards
the pressure goes in, inside the other word

parts.note: routs are heavy defeats
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Stress from crushing losses lifted a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes into ROUTS to make ROPUTS, which 'lifted' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near unconsciousness or bewilderment, much like a daze.

clue.text: Smell found in empty canals and small streams

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located inside the other
empty means the inside letters go, leaving the outside ones of canals

parts.note: reek means a strong smell

explanation.surface: A stink rising from drained canals and brooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeks are narrow inlets or brooks, small streams of water.

clue.text: Assign a value to degree

definitions.meaning: to judge something's worth or rank it
a level or speed, as in 'at a fast pace'

explanation.surface: Place a value on a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to evaluate something; a rate is also a measure or level, as in the rate of growth.

clue.text: Make no progress, in the main

definitions.text: Make no progress, in the main

parts.words: Make no progress, in the main
parts.note: a swimmer in the sea (the main) who stays upright and kicks in place makes no headway; the phrase also means stagnating generally

explanation.surface: Stand still out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea, so the clue pictures a swimmer staying in one spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to mark time without advancing, literally to stay afloat upright without swimming anywhere.

clue.text: Range limited by African desert

indicators.note: limited by means the letters are held within the bounds of these words

explanation.surface: Mountains bordered by an African desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants an African range, but the mountains are in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes is the great mountain range of South America.

clue.text: Check on oxygen embargo

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the check comes first

parts.note: to vet is to check
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An inspection of oxygen leads to a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a prohibition or ban, as an embargo is.

clue.text: Planned study assignment and read regularly

parts.note: a project is a piece of schoolwork or study set as an assignment

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word read is taken

explanation.surface: A student organised a coursework piece and kept up the reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of 'read', E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Projected means forecast or scheduled, as in projected costs, so it fits planned.

clue.text: Regret keeping vacant place for Indian bread

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: rue means regret

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of place

explanation.surface: Someone regrets saving an empty seat for a naan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, so Indian bread is a currency, not a flatbread.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, and bread is slang for money.

clue.text: Informed about old English hotel getting a grip

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the other pieces are placed inside

parts.note: informed means told
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Briefed on an ancient English inn, someone finally gets a footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting' is a link; 'about' has TOLD surround O, E and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small foothold or grip, literally space for the toes when climbing.

clue.text: Pressure now on board finding areas of activity

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside it, so the other pieces go within

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the vessel one boards
P is the symbol for pressure
here can mean now, as in 'here we go'

explanation.surface: Stress at sea is turning up domains of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field or domain of interest, such as a sphere of influence.
